Create Your Hero

Begin with a person you want to play: an armored healer, an eloquent duelist, a hunter who speaks with ghosts. Decide what they want, then choose how they pursue it.

Character creation has two stages. Level 0 is your life before choosing a class. Level 1 is the completed adventurer you bring to the first session. Finish and close the level-0 ledger before making level-1 purchases. Both stages have their own DP pool; unused points expire separately.

Before making purchases, turn to @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.f96a6421bb52ac90.JournalEntryPage.b84fcd9536c51a01]{Disciplines and Character Paths}. It explains what discipline ranks mean and how they qualify you for abilities. Keep that chapter and your intended class entry handy as you build.

1. Assign attributes

Assign a value from −2 to +2 to each of the six attributes. Their total must be +3. A straightforward starting array is +2, +1, +1, +0, +0, −1, arranged as you choose. Check your intended class's minimums before settling the array.

AttributeCommon uses
BrawnExert strength, use Force, climb and make many melee attacks.
FortitudeEndure harm, resist bodily threats and make death rolls; contributes to HP.
AgilityMove deftly, remain Hidden, jump and make many ranged attacks; contributes to Speed.
GuileDeceive, misdirect, improvise and exploit an opening.
KnowledgeApply learning, recognize patterns, craft and use learned techniques.
ReasonNotice details, perceive danger, judge a situation and keep your thinking clear.

These are not exclusive lists. Roll the attribute printed on the ability you use. Some techniques deliberately use an unusual attribute, such as Knowledge for a carefully studied attack. There is no added skill rating.

Your chosen attributes stay fixed as you gain levels. Explicit items can modify an attribute while their rules apply. Ordinary published item adjustments run no higher than +2 or lower than −2, but can move your total outside the creation range. Matching bonuses do not add together: use the largest. A curse can explicitly suppress bonuses or set a value instead. Item changes never revise your creation DP.

2. Choose ancestry

Choose Human, Elf, Dwarf or Halfling. Record the ancestry's HP contribution and base Speed, then choose two of its five traits. Read the exact benefits: a description of keen eyes does not grant an extra sense unless the rules say so.

AncestryHP contributionBase SpeedStarting coin contribution
Human+26+1
Elf+26+2
Dwarf+45+2
Halfling+15+0

Any ancestry can grow up in any culture. Your ancestry is not a compulsory profession, personality or allegiance.

3. Choose culture and background

Your culture describes the community that shaped you. Your background describes part of your life or work before adventuring. Choose one of each from the origin chapter, then select one complete paired option from each. A pair grants a rank-1 discipline and its accompanying ability. Do not take the rank from one pair and the ability from another.

A granted ability supplies its stated prerequisite grants. Record the ranks before buying anything. If a grant duplicates something you already have, receive 1 DP for that stage. It does not raise the rank, give an unrestricted replacement, or carry forward after the stage ends.

Record Common and one ordinary language learned in your home community, then apply explicit extra language grants. See @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.b65e9644d24629f2.JournalEntryPage.0237eee3512bbfa9]{Languages} for the shared list, spoken-only grants and campaign alternatives.

4. Spend level-0 DP

Your level-0 pool is 10 + Knowledge + Reason + Guile, plus any duplicate-grant compensation. Negative attributes reduce this pool too. Buy eligible Novice abilities at their printed price: normally 2 DP, or 1 DP for the six shared exceptions in @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.3944c923ee8b4968.JournalEntryPage.efd0799a6387e823]{Abilities}. Their printed requirements must already be met by your origin grants. You may not buy discipline ranks at level 0.

Record each purchase in order. Buy any eligible kind of ability. One or two attacks can define your fighting style, leaving room for talents useful between battles. If you have an odd point left, a 1-DP ability can put it to use; these choices remain available at later levels too.

Close the stage. Unused level-0 DP expires. Your future class cannot qualify a purchase you made earlier.

5. Choose a class

Choose one class. Both of its required attributes must be at least 0; Odd has no minimums. Record its HP contribution and discipline prices. Choose two distinct rank-1 disciplines from its starting list, applying duplicate compensation where appropriate. Choose one of its three level-1 signature abilities.

Your class sets discipline prices and signature access. You can buy any eligible shared ability. There is no multiclassing.

6. Spend level-1 DP

Start a new pool of 10 + Knowledge + Reason + Guile, plus level-1 duplicate compensation. Now you can purchase discipline ranks at your class's prices as well as eligible abilities. You must buy ranks sequentially: rank 2 requires owning rank 1, and rank 3 requires owning rank 2. There is no additional level gate on ranks.

Your class entry lists the price of every discipline rank. The comparison table in @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.f96a6421bb52ac90.JournalEntryPage.b84fcd9536c51a01]{Disciplines and Character Paths} shows all classes together. Each price buys that rank alone. For example, a Blade pays 1 DP for Arms 1 and 2 DP for Arms 2, spending 3 DP to learn both from scratch. A rank grants no action or bonus by itself; it qualifies you to learn abilities.

All card prerequisites must be owned before purchase, not merely before use. You can own an item whose requirements you do not meet, but cannot use the gated capability. A flaming sword's special power does not become available simply because you found it.

Close the stage. Unused level-1 DP expires. Later levels allow saving DP.

> Example — two separate budgets. A hero with Knowledge +1, Reason +1 and Guile −1 > gets 11 DP at each creation stage. At level 0, five Novice purchases cost 10 and > the last point expires. At level 1, a duplicate class rank adds 1 to the new pool, > making 12. Buying a discipline rank priced at 3 DP and four Novice cards for 8 spends 11; > the remaining point also expires. Nothing from the first stage was borrowed.

7. Resolve equipment and recipes

Read every acquisition line. Some learned cards grant an ordinary item when first acquired. A grant supplies the compatible basic item only if you do not already own it. Three attacks that require a melee weapon can share the same weapon; they do not generate three free weapons. The same principle applies when you learn training later. Selling an item does not reactivate its old grant.

Describe your weapon now. A sword, axe or stout staff can express the same permitted melee attacks. Its ordinary appearance changes no damage. A ranged attack still requires compatible ranged equipment. Most ordinary melee and ranged weapons use 1 Bulk each. Special items add only their printed effects.

Choose any recipes explicitly granted by crafting cards. Recipe knowledge is not a free finished product or a supply of ingredients. Record tools, materials and future recipe opportunities separately.

8. Finish your numbers

RecordCalculation
Maximum HP12 + ancestry HP + class HP + Fortitude + explicit benefits
Capacity10 + 3 × Brawn
EncumbranceCarried Bulk above capacity, minimum 0
SpeedAncestry base + Agility − encumbrance, minimum 0
Stability0 unless an explicit grant raises it; highest source, cap 3
Starting Grit2, plus any explicitly purchased increase
Starting wounds / death marks0 / 0

HP does not automatically grow each level. A purchase such as Conditioned Body can increase it within that card's limits. Record current and maximum HP separately. Record your highest resistance for each damage type, never a sum of matching armor.

> Example — Borin's pack. Borin is a dwarf Protector with Fortitude +2. His base > maximum HP is 12 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 23. His chosen trait and Conditioned Body each add > 1, giving 25. Brawn +1 gives capacity 13. His 11 Bulk fits, so Agility +0 leaves > his dwarf base Speed at 5. Armor does not automatically add Stability.

9. Take coins and shop

Starting coins are 40 + ancestry + culture + background + class contributions. The Starting Coins reference at the end of this chapter gives the exact additions. This produces 50–70 coins before shopping. Resolve equipment grants first. Everyone begins with a plain worn outfit; a pack, supplies and potion are purchases unless explicitly granted.

Use the market. Record coins spent, coins left, supply dice and every item's Bulk. A container does not cancel its contents' Bulk. Decide which items are held. A bow, a two-handed weapon, or weapon and shield can leave no free hand for healing. Sharing a rope or light is practical; somebody still carries it.

10. Put a person on the sheet

Name your hero and give them a reason to stay with the party. Put your most-used actions on your first reference page. All learned cards remain available; there is no prepared-card hand limit.

Before play, check both DP ledgers, requirements, grants, Bulk, free hands and class minimums. The six complete characters near the back show every step.

Growing into a legend

The DA awards levels at milestones. At level 2 and every later level, receive 8 + your new level DP. Save these points or spend them in a place the DA agrees is safe. Mental attributes modify only the two creation pools, not these awards.

New levelDP awardOther universal milestone
210—
311+1 Grit; choose a level-3 class signature; Adept cards available
412—
513—
614—
715+1 Grit; choose a level-7 class signature; Master cards available
816—
917—
1018—

Novice, Adept and Master abilities normally cost 2, 4 and 8 DP and require minimum levels 1, 3 and 7. Novice purchases are explicitly permitted during level-0 creation. The six shared 1-DP abilities keep their printed price at every level. Higher tiers do not require an earlier card in a chain. Mixed requirements mean you need every listed rank. Class signatures require only their class and level; extra eligible signatures can be purchased for the same tier price.

Your Grit increases are universal experience, not class features. They do not refund previous expenditure. A once-only learned card can grant one additional Grit. Ordinary rest does not refresh Grit. Your abilities, scars and choices tell the story of the hero you become.
